lead: Contacts on scanner near {destination}.
Three ships drop out of cruise dead ahead.
The scanner lights up with hulls that were not there a minute ago.
turn: They were waiting for you.
Somebody sold your route.
They have your heading and your speed, which nobody should.
note: Someone talked. {client} swears it wasn't them.
The ambushers knew the schedule. That's worth asking {client} about.
Pirates do not turn up this prepared by luck.
close: You keep the receipts and the dents.
Check the transponder logs before you take another job.
Word of it will be in the next system before you are.

description: Text for the 'Creditors in the dark' complication.

lead: A hail comes in on an open channel, polite and very calm.
Two ships take position either side of you and match your speed.
A tug-class hull cuts across your path and does not apologise.
turn: They are not pirates. They are collectors, and they think {client} is aboard or paying you.
They want to know where {client}'s money has gone, and they have brought guns to ask.
They hold a paper claim on everything {client} owns, and you are carrying some of it.
note: {client} left out that the debts were this old, or this armed.
The collectors have your ship's registry now. They will remember.
Nobody mentioned creditors in the briefing. {client} had a lot of unmentioned things.
close: Ask for danger pay next time, in writing.
At least the collectors were tidy about it.
{client} sends their regrets. Regrets don't repair hulls.

lead: Fast ships, no markings, closing from the {system} lane.
A burst of drive flare off the starboard quarter. Someone has been following for a while.
Your scanner picks up a wing of light fighters that did not come from {system}.
turn: Their lead pilot says only: 'Nothing personal. Somebody else wants this job.'
They go for your engines first. They want you late, not necessarily dead.
They fly like people paid by the day, careful and not willing to die for it.
note: Someone bought this ambush. Somebody with money wanted you out of the way.
The pilots were hired talent. The one who hired them is still out there.
A rival knew you had the job before you left dock.
close: Make a note of whoever gained from it.
Wages for hired guns run out faster than grudges do.
You will see that wing again.

lead: A distress beacon wakes on your channel, weak and repeating.
A drifting hull shows on scanner near {destination}, lights dark, hatch open.
A ship begs for help on a frequency only spacers use.
turn: The hull is a decoy. The engines you hear powering up belong to the crew hiding behind it.
Whoever is calling is not stranded. They are fishing, and you are the catch.
As you slow to help, three more signatures come alive around the wreck.
note: It is an old pirate trick. It still works because spacers still stop.
Next time somebody calls for help, be sure first. Then be sure again.
The hull was real once. Its crew was not aboard.
close: Even so, you slowed down. Most captains would.
The beacon is still out there, calling.
Nobody can say how many ships have answered it.

lead: A port scan flags your {cargo} as stolen property.
The {cargo} carries serials that match a convoy reported missing.
A customs officer holds up a scanner reading and says nothing for a long time.
turn: You are now wanted.
Somebody listed you as the thief, and the paperwork is very good.
The real owner has already filed, and {faction} takes theft seriously.
note: {faction} won't be offering you work for a while.
You were the delivery, and also the scapegoat.
Whoever stole it is two systems away and richer.
close: Check serials before you load next time.
{client} claims to have bought the lot in good faith.
The cargo is somebody's, just not {client}'s.

description: Text for the 'Seal of the holds' complication.

lead: Under the crate wrap, a hold seal. It was meant to be scraped off.
A dwarf inspector at the dock turns your {cargo} over and reads the stamp aloud.
The manifest says one thing. The stamp on the {cargo} says a hold in the Drift, and a lot number that was reported lost.
turn: Holds register everything, and they never forget a lot number.
A dwarf reads a stamp the way other people read a confession.
The hold has already filed a claim with the Gate Authority.
note: The hold wants its goods back and an apology in writing.
Dwarves sue slowly and exactly. Expect a letter.
{client} bought the {cargo} off a man with a good smile and no receipts.
close: Contracts are sacred, and you broke one without knowing it.
The seal will outlast the paperwork.
The hold lost the shipment months ago and has been counting ever since.

lead: An enforcement cutter hails you with a seizure order, apologetic and firm.
Your scanner finds a seized-goods tag under a layer of fresh paint.
A patrol officer reads the lot code and then reads it again.
turn: The {cargo} was impounded by {faction} and spirited out of the yard before the paperwork closed.
It was never legally released. Someone just wrote 'released' on it.
You are carrying property that the state believes it still owns.
note: The yard clerk who signed it out has vanished.
{faction} wants an explanation. You have one, and no one believes it.
It was a clever fraud. You were the transport.
close: The only winner is the clerk, who is not on any manifest.
Keep your copy of the contract. It is your best defence.
{client} had a very good story prepared.

lead: An insurer's investigator is waiting at {destination}.
A message from a claims office finds you first.
Your scan comes back clean, which is odd, because the {cargo} has already been paid out.
turn: The {cargo} was written off as lost in transit. Somebody collected, then sold it again.
If it arrives, the claim is fraud and the fraudster is whoever signed the manifest.
Its owner would rather it stayed at the bottom of a gravity well.
note: The investigator wants a statement and your ship logs.
You were hired to move evidence of a crime that you didn't commit.
{client} has gone very quiet.
close: Insurers are patient. They will find the others involved.
Keep copies of everything.
Not your fraud. Still your name on the form.

description: Text for the 'The money isn't there' complication.

lead: You reach {destination} and ask for payment.
The transfer bounces with a polite error code.
At the handover, {client}'s representative hands you a smaller case than you were promised.
turn: #voice:payment# It turns out they meant a different number.
The account is real. The funds in it are not.
'Of course you'll be paid,' says the representative. 'Eventually.'
note: {client} owes you the reward, and you are not the only one waiting.
You can chase them, or you can write it off.
Lesson recorded: ask for half up front.
close: The reward will come late or never.
Collecting will cost more than it's worth.
There are other captains in the queue ahead of you.

description: Text for the 'Someone else's job' complication.

lead: Something about the handover at {destination} is off.
The contact at {destination} does not know {client}.
A second party appears and asks, politely, why you're doing this.
turn: {client} was a front. The real employer is {faction}, and they didn't want it known.
The person who hired you is a broker, and the person who pays is someone you would have refused.
Your client's name was borrowed. The real one is worse.
note: Nothing illegal, as far as you can tell. Nothing honest either.
You did the work. Nobody asked you to like who it was for.
{faction} now knows your ship, your name and your rates.
close: The money cleared, which is something.
You will be asked back. You may not want to be.
Expect a handshake from people who don't shake hands.

description: Text for the 'The quiet route' complication.

lead: The route is not what you were told.
The trouble starts a jump early.
You find the first wreck an hour out of {system}.
turn: Others have run this route before you. None of them are still running it.
{client} said the lane was clear. The lane has a toll collector and a gun.
The danger was real, known and left out of the briefing.
note: {client} did not warn you because they could not afford a captain who would say no.
The reward was fair for the job you were told about, and unfair for this one.
A competent captain checks the route. You did. The route changed.
close: Add a risk fee to your next quote.
Ask other captains before you sign.
#voice:closer#

description: Text for the 'Not what was said' complication.

lead: The briefing and the situation at {destination} do not match.
You find out what the job is really for.
A passing comment from a dock worker rearranges everything you thought you knew.
turn: {client} wanted it done as a cover for something else.
It was never a simple run. It was a distraction, and you were a decent one.
What you carried or did was not the point. Where you were seen was the point.
note: Somewhere else, {client} got what they wanted while all eyes were on you.
You can't prove it. You also can't forget it.
The reward looks smaller now, and the favour looks bigger.
close: Don't take the next offer from {client} without asking why.
Everyone has a reason. Few share it.
At least the pay is real.

lead: Word reaches you at the dock: another captain has been in to see {client}.
A rival's ship sits at the next berth with its engines already warm.
A message from {client} arrives in the middle of your preparations.
turn: They have offered to do the job for less, and {client} has noticed.
They are heading for {destination} now, and the first one there gets paid.
It is a race, and the winner is the one who gets the signature.
note: Whoever arrives second goes home with an empty hold and a story.
{client} loves a bidding war. It saves them money.
Nobody likes being the one who lost.
close: Rivals have long memories.
There is always another captain.
You know their name now.

lead: A second ship docks at {destination} at the same time as you.
The contact looks from you to the other captain, and then at the floor.
Two sets of papers, the same signature, and one reward between them.
turn: {client} sold the contract twice and hoped one of you wouldn't arrive.
Neither of you is lying, which makes it worse.
There is one payment, and it's {reward}.
note: You and the other captain split a drink and a grievance.
The pay may be halved. Or one of you finishes first.
{client} says it was a misunderstanding.
close: Misunderstandings cost money.
You made a friend, possibly.
Do not work for {client} again without a deposit.

lead: A {faction} ship has taken your berth.
A faction officer appears with a letter of preference.
The dock has been politely cleared, and you are no longer first in line.
turn: {faction} has leaned on {client}. The job will be done by one of their own.
They'd rather not be seen blocking you, so they have simply arrived first.
They have more guns than you, and better manners.
note: You did the work anyway, or you did not. Either way, {faction} will remember.
A competitor with a flag is hard to beat.
{client} apologised. It cost them nothing.
close: Fly under a different flag next time.
Politics eats jobs.
It is not personal, which is worse.

lead: A noise in the service crawlway. Not a rat.
The life support readout shows one more body than you carried.
Your crew drags someone out of a locker near the airlock.
turn: They are running from {faction}, and will not say why.
They are begging you not to dock at {destination}.
There's a bounty on them. The sum is not small.
note: They went their own way at the next port. You never learned their name.
{faction} knows they were on your ship.
It was kinder than it was smart.
close: You will be remembered by someone, for something.
Either you did a good deed or a stupid one.
Nobody has put a price on you. Yet.

lead: A scan at {destination} flags a name on your manifest.
A patrol hails you and asks to see your papers in particular.
A wanted notice in the port feed carries a face you recognise.
turn: {faction} has a warrant out for someone you are moving.
The person you are here for is wanted. You are now an accessory.
{client} left out the charges.
note: You can hand them over or run. Each costs something.
Whatever {client} promised, the law does not care.
The reward was good. The record is not.
close: Never ask a client about a charge you do not want to hear.
The paperwork will chase you for weeks.
It was only ever a matter of time.

lead: A very patient man is waiting for you at {destination}.
A lender's ship has been following you since {system}.
A message arrives for someone who is meant to be unnamed.
turn: The one in your care owes a lot, to someone who has run out of patience.
They have run before. This time they ran onto your ship.
{client} didn't mention that anyone would be chasing.
note: A debt is not a crime. It still gets people hurt.
You can leave them to the lender or you can stand in the way.
The lender is polite about it. That is the frightening part.
close: Debts follow people better than ships do.
You gave them a head start.
They will remember the kindness.

lead: An unlisted ship follows your wake out of {system} and keeps its distance.
Someone aboard is sweating through every scan.
A long-range hail offers you a fortune to turn back.
turn: They saw something at {destination}. The people who would prefer they hadn't are very near.
They know a name. The name belongs to {faction}.
They are the only living witness, and you are the only ship.
note: You can protect them, or you can sell them. You made your choice.
{faction} won't forget how you answered.
Some jobs turn into a fight for the right reasons.
close: Better to see nothing and say less.
A quiet life is not on offer.
Make sure you can still explain it later.

description: Text for the 'Paid to lose you' complication.

lead: Docking at {destination}, you find the berth guarded and the guards not looking at you.
The handover is a trap.
{client}'s contact is smiling too widely.
turn: The job was a pretext. The real buyer was someone who wants your ship.
{client} sold you out for more than {reward}.
Whoever is waiting at {destination} was told exactly when you would arrive.
note: {client} thinks you will not come back. They are mistaken.
You walked out of it. Barely.
The reward is gone. The grudge isn't.
close: You will see {client} again, in their own time.
Keep your wits and your ship.
Betrayal is simply another line on the invoice.

lead: The reward is on the table at {destination}, and it is not {reward}.
{client}'s agent slides a revised contract across the desk.
A small clause you didn't write has appeared in your copy.
turn: The new figure is smaller. 'Costs,' they say. 'Unforeseen.'
They hold your cargo, passengers or goods until you sign.
Whatever you do, you do it under their guns.
note: You signed, or you did not. Either way, someone made a point.
The price of integrity is occasionally a lot.
{client} is not the type to apologise.
close: Read the amendments. Then read them again.
Take your evidence to whoever will listen.
It is a mean trick, and it works often.

description: Text for the 'The fall guy' complication.

lead: The job goes without a hitch, which should have worried you.
As you undock from {destination}, the alarms start.
A patrol cutter closes before you clear the lane.
turn: Someone planted evidence. Your ship's name is all over it.
{client} needed a scapegoat, and your transponder was handy.
Whatever happened at {destination}, it was blamed on you.
note: {faction} has your name now. You will have to clear it.
The real culprit has {reward} of yours and a good alibi.
It is hard to prove a negative.
close: Always keep logs. Always.
Some jobs exist only to be blamed on someone.
A clear conscience is not the same as a clear record.

description: Text for the 'The sealed case' complication.

lead: A deckhand finds a sealed case behind a service panel.
A gate warden's scan picks up a shape that is not on your manifest.
Something in the ship is warm when it should be cold.
turn: The case isn't on any manifest. It holds goods that are illegal on this side of the gate.
Someone hid it aboard to ride through the gate unchecked.
Whatever is in it, it is worth a great deal to someone.
note: You can dump it, report it or deliver it. Each has a price.
It was planted by someone who knew your route.
{faction} would pay well to learn where it came from.
close: Check every panel before departure.
Nobody claimed it. Nobody will.
A smuggler's gift, and a smuggler's problem.

lead: A gate warden's scan lingers on your engine bay.
A diagnostic reports a component that is not in your ship's specification.
Your engineer asks quietly whether you have been refitted.
turn: There is rim tech aboard, built into the hull where nobody would look.
It is old and elegant and it does not belong on a ship this side of the last good gate.
The Lantern Synod will pay a lot to learn how it got there.
note: Nobody can say who put it there.
You stripped it out. The ship runs worse, and you sleep better.
The warden pretended not to see. That was a kindness, or a mark.
close: Some questions are better not asked.
Rim tech is never just rim tech.
You will be scanned twice as hard from now on.

lead: A customs officer at {destination} asks to open a small bag.
A sniffer drone circles you at the dock and settles over one locker.
A routine inspection takes much longer than it should.
turn: Inside is something very illegal, and it has your signature on the loading slip.
It was given to you by someone at {system} who said it was a favour.
The goods are worth more than the job itself.
note: You talked your way out, mostly.
{client} claims to know nothing, and sounds convincing.
The officer let you go with a warning and a fine.
close: Never take a bag from a stranger.
A fine is cheaper than a cell.
You will be searched again.

lead: The gate at {system} is closed for inspection.
A queue of waiting ships stretches back from the gate mouth.
A notice goes up at the gate: delays of unknown length.
turn: You have {deadline} on the clock and no way through.
The Gate Authority will not say when it will reopen.
You can wait, or you can pay for a slot, or you can find another way round.
note: You made it, or you did not. In either case, the Gate Authority sent a bill.
Gates keep their own time and answer to no schedule.
The delay cost you time and a little pride.
close: Factor in gate delays next time.
Nobody has ever got a refund from the Authority.
Some of the queue got through. Some turned round.

lead: A message from {client} reaches you at {system}.
Another ship brings word from {client}, nine days old.
{client}'s agent catches you at the dock.
turn: #voice:urgency# The deadline has moved up.
It has been cut to less than you have left, and there is no appeal.
Something has changed on their side, and they will not tell you what.
note: You pushed the drive and paid for it later.
The reward holds, but the margin does not.
{client} did not say thank you.
close: Ask what changed. Ask early.
Drive wear is a cost too.
Some clients live in a permanent hurry.

lead: Word reaches you by a passing freighter.
A courier ship brings the latest from {client}.
The newsfeed at {system} is days old and says something about your contract.
turn: The brief you were working from was out of date. You have far less time than you thought.
Nobody told you the job changed, because nobody could.
There is no faster-than-light radio, and that is an old problem.
note: There is nobody to blame, which is the annoying part.
You did what you could with what you had.
Distance makes liars of honest people.
close: Every plan is a few days old by the time you act.
The galaxy is wide and slow.
Carry some slack.

lead: A {faction} patrol orders you to stop at a station off your route.
Flags at the gate: all ships to the checkpoint.
A military cutter blocks the lane and gestures to a nearby dock.
turn: You are held while they go through the ship, slowly and in great detail.
The inspection finds nothing. It also takes a day.
It is routine, they say. They say that to everyone.
note: You lost time and some patience.
{faction} stamped your papers and moved on.
Nobody explained the reason, and you did not ask.
close: Bring good paperwork.
Law thins at the edge and thickens at checkpoints.
The delay was within the contract. Only just.

description: Text for the 'One more thing' complication.

lead: A message from {client} arrives mid-route.
{client} calls with a request that cannot be refused politely.
At {system}, a contact flags you down.
turn: They want you to stop and pick up one more thing before {destination}.
It is a small favour, and an unpaid one.
They say it is on the way. It is not.
note: It took time and it cost fuel.
You collected it. You decided not to ask what it was.
{client} says thanks, and means it, a little.
close: Extra stops should come with extra pay.
Say no sometimes.
Favours are the currency of people with no money.

lead: A ship with a failed drive hails you near {system}.
A tow request on a frequency you cannot ignore.
A freighter drifts dead in the lane, hazard lights flashing.
turn: The captain asks you to tow them to the nearest port, or to carry a spare part.
It is a real emergency. You can tell from the voices.
They have little to offer except gratitude and a story.
note: It cost time. It may even have saved lives.
They said they would remember you.
You will be told this story at a bar one day.
close: Space is large and cold. Be kind where you can.
The gratitude was genuine.
The clock kept running regardless.

lead: The charts for {destination} are months old.
What {client} told you about {destination} no longer holds.
You arrive and find the system has changed hands.
turn: Someone else claimed it since. They do not welcome visitors.
There is a new station, a new tariff and a new set of guns.
The people you were told to find are gone.
note: You made the best of it.
Old information is worse than none.
The galaxy keeps moving whether or not you do.
close: Check the charts. Then check who made them.
Everything is out of date by the time it is written.
It could have been worse.

lead: There is nothing at the coordinates {client} gave you.
The scan at {destination} shows empty space.
The station you were sent to does not answer.
turn: Either the numbers were wrong or somebody wanted you looking in the wrong place.
You are in the right system and the wrong half of it.
There is nobody here, and there never was.
note: It took time to find the right place.
You are still not sure whether it was a mistake.
Cheap intelligence has cost you.
close: Question your sources.
Maps lie. People lie more.
The galaxy is mostly empty, and today it felt like it.

description: Text for the 'Not so quiet' complication.

lead: Scans at {destination} read far more hulls than expected.
The 'quiet backwater' turns out to have a navy picket.
A defence grid you had not been told about comes alive.
turn: Whoever supplied the briefing was out of date, or lying, or paid to be wrong.
You were told lightly guarded. It's not.
The job just got harder, and the reward did not change.
note: You adjusted, or you ran.
Someone should hear about this.
It was close.
close: Bring more firepower than the briefing says.
A cheap tip is the most expensive kind.
Intelligence is only worth what you pay for it.

description: Text for the 'A better offer' complication.

lead: A message reaches you, unsigned but well funded.
At the dock a stranger orders two drinks and sits down.
A courier brings a sealed offer.
turn: Walk away from {client}'s contract and keep a share of the reward as a gift.
They will pay you more to do nothing than {client} will to do the work.
They want you to fail, and they will pay well for it.
note: You took it, or you didn't. Both have consequences.
Loyalty is a currency too.
The offer stood for exactly as long as you needed to doubt it.
close: Nobody makes an offer like that for nothing.
Remember who asked.
It is a fair price for a clean conscience.

lead: A {faction} envoy requests a private word.
A {faction} ship hails you with a polite request.
You are invited to dinner by someone with a flag.
turn: They will pay you to hand the result to them instead of {client}.
{faction} wants what you are carrying or what you know, and they are generous.
Refusing is possible. It will not be comfortable.
note: You made your choice.
{client} may find out, or may not.
{faction} is a useful friend and a dangerous one.
close: Choose your friends carefully.
Reputation is slow to build.
The money is real. So is the risk.

description: Text for the 'Share the work' complication.

lead: Another captain pulls alongside and asks for a word.
A hail comes in from a ship headed for {destination}.
A rival you know is waiting in the lane.
turn: They want to split the reward and take the risk together.
They will cover the dangerous half if you cover the rest.
It is an honest offer from an honest rival, which is rare.
note: It worked, or it didn't.
You split the reward and the grievance.
It is nice, now and then, to have company.
close: Not everyone is an enemy.
Keep an eye on them anyway.
Cooperation is rarer than it looks.

description: Text for the 'Your own voice' complication.

lead: A hail comes in from nowhere on the channel you were using.
The comm crackles near {system}.
A ship you cannot see answers your call sign.
turn: It is your voice. It says what you were about to say.
It uses your name, {captain}, and the pitch of your own breath.
It stops mid-sentence, as if it had heard enough.
note: Nobody else heard it. You checked.
You logged it and it was gone from the log in the morning.
Nothing came of it. That is the part you keep returning to.
close: The recorder was empty.
You told no one.
It did not come again. You stay off that channel.

lead: Every screen shows static at once.
The comms drop to a low, regular pulse.
Instruments freeze and then drift, all in agreement.
turn: The static has a rhythm. It is not random. It is not a language either.
Your crew stops speaking, one by one, and nobody notices.
It lasts exactly as long as it takes you to start to worry.
note: Afterwards the clocks disagree by a few minutes.
Nobody can say what it was.
You are careful not to ask the engineer.
close: The ship is fine. The ship is always fine.
It is quiet out here, and not always empty.
You did not mention it at port.

lead: The gate at {system} lights up before you have asked it to.
The gate ring dims and brightens in a slow cycle.
The gate passes you through and then shows a second, empty arrival.
turn: It opens to a place that is not on your route, and then it opens to the right one.
The warden's console says no traffic. You are in the traffic.
For a moment you can see something else on the far side. Then you cannot.
note: The Gate Authority has no record of anything unusual.
Gates do things nobody understands. This was one of them.
You did not slow down. You are glad you didn't.
close: The gate was never the problem.
It looked at you, if a gate can.
You will take another route next time.

lead: A transponder pings on your scanner, clear and strong.
The registry says the ship was lost a year ago.
A familiar hull-ident appears off {destination} and stays on your tail.
turn: The ship is not there. The signal is. It follows you the whole way.
It answers every hail with the same four words.
When you finally turn to look, the scanner is empty and the log is full.
note: You reported it. They said it was a ghost signal, and left it at that.
Another captain heard it too, they said, in the same lane.
There are a lot of missing ships on the rim, and not all of them stay missing.
close: Some signals are better ignored.
It was never found.
You take the long way round now.
